model_note: Meadows' 12 leverage points, numbered as in ~/learning/Notes/Leverage Points — where to intervene in a system.md (1 = weakest: constants/parameters; 8 = rules; 10 = goals; 11 = paradigm; 12 = power to transcend paradigms). Each finding below names the level its intervention sits at.
summary: The single highest-leverage change is a LEVEL-10 (goals) one: the gauntlet's definition of 'lane done' currently cannot be satisfied by anything on screen, and the lane that is mandatorily FIRST (L0) is the only lane in the 12-lane board whose entire gate is markdown-document integrity. That one ordering sentence at docs/GAUNTLET.md:139 plus ruling R2 at :338 is what has held src/ frozen for 27 days across 58 commits. Everything else the review is likely to reach for — agent counts, batch widths, one-workflow rules, new hooks — is Meadows level 1-8 and pushes near the hinge. Ranked: F1 goals (level 10, carried by a deletion), F2 structure of flows (level 3, needs no rule at all), F3 loop gain (level 6). Deliberately NOT proposed: the reference/ backup question (level 3, and assigned to the Margin of Safety lens) and 'let agents amend the lane board' (level 9, no defensible concrete edit — it would be an opinion).

findings.claim: MEADOWS LEVEL 10 (GOALS) — THE ANSWER. The gauntlet's objective function is ledger truth, not playable surface: the lane that gates all eleven others is the only lane whose 'done' cannot be satisfied by anything a player could see, and deleting its mandatory-first ordering is the single change that moves the most.
findings.cite: docs/GAUNTLET.md:139 and :338 (ordering rule + R2); scripts/gauntlet/gateL0.py:9-14 (all six L0 gate items); commit c2e5df9 (2026-08-13, engine adopted); commit 0719673 (2026-07-28, last src/ change)

And the queue still pointed at that markdown file (RESUME_HERE.md 'What is left, in order'): WF-4 dry-loop 13-25 agents + l0-rewrite 42 agents = 55-67 MORE agents before the ordering rule releases any other lane.

WHY THIS IS LEVEL 10 AND NOT LEVEL 8: 'L0 first, always' reads like a rule, but what it encodes is the system's objective — the map must be provably true before the territory is touched. A rule constrains behaviour inside a goal; the definition of DONE *is* the goal, because it is the only thing the whole engine optimises toward. Every lower-level lever in this repo has already been pulled and the output variable did not move: batch width 24->7 (8f332e9, level 1), agents 2->9 and 28->42 (3adac1b, level 1), one-workflow-in-flight (7476add, level 8), fail-closed accounting (level 8). Fifty-eight commits of level-1-to-8 intervention produced zero movement in the thing the project exists to produce. That is the signature of pushing near the hinge.

WHY IT IS ALSO A LEVEL-11 (PARADIGM) FINDING: §0's artifact table lists A5 — Kheshav's own LOOK verdict — LAST, as one of five equal artifacts (docs/GAUNTLET.md:52). A1-A4 (frame, payload row, byte-check, ledger number) can each be re-contested by the next agent forever; A5 is the only artifact in the system that cannot be re-litigated. The game is DEAD (§0), so there is no attainable ground truth beyond the frames and the payload — which means a truth standard built only on A1-A4 has no terminator by construction. The t1 fixed point (LEV-3) is not a workflow bug; it is that paradigm's signature, and SALVAGE.md names it in its own words: the excluded claims are 'refinements of refinements'. Promoting A5 from fifth-of-five to the clause every gate ends in is what makes lanes terminate.
findings.rule_targeted: docs/GAUNTLET.md §2 'Ordering rule' (:139), §5 paste-ready prompt (:264), §6 ruling R2 (:338-341)
findings.proposed_change:
THREE DELETIONS AND ONE CLAUSE.
(1) DELETE ruling R2 in full, docs/GAUNTLET.md:338-341 (50 words, measured). R2's stated protection — 'planning lanes off it would send agents to frame-count numbers we already hold' — is ALREADY delivered, independent of ordering, by :85: 'Any lane that frame-counts a number the payload states outright has failed its own gate.' R2 protects nothing that :85 does not.
(2) DELETE 'L0 first, always. Then' from :139 (4 words) and '(L0 first if it hasn't run)' from :264 (6 words).
(3) The ordering rule becomes: '**Ordering rule:** highest (leverage ÷ risk). No lane closes on a document alone — every lane's gate ends in an A5 LOOK on a changed screen.' (19 words added.)
NET -41 WORDS, so it pays for LEV-3 and still clears ARCH-E.
INCIDENT IT WOULD HAVE PREVENTED: 58 commits since 2026-08-12, zero touching src/ (pasted above) — under this gate, L0 could not have closed without a screen change, so the 11-day 51-commit ledger drive would have had to interleave with the L2/L3 generators.
SECOND-ORDER CONSEQUENCE, HONESTLY STATED: the owner's eye becomes the scheduler and the single bottleneck. He is the only A5 authority and cannot be parallelised, so lanes will queue behind his attention instead of behind agent budget — that is a real cost and it is the RIGHT cost, because his attention is the only thing in this system that can end a verification regress. §2 already routes L5/L6 to interleave 'whenever the owner's LOOK queue has an open verdict'; this generalises that to all twelve.
ROLLBACK: restore the four deleted lines from commit 2df2f87 — `git checkout 2df2f87 -- docs/GAUNTLET.md`.
DOES NOT VIOLATE §6 WHAT NOT TO TOUCH: §6 permits re-planning lane L0 and forbids only invalidating its banked data. The 1,693 judged claims, 553 overturns and run2..run16 stay exactly where they are; only the ORDER in which the remaining 55-67 agents are spent changes.

LEV-2 cannot be executed without LEV-1 being decided. A change that must wait on another change is by definition the lower-leverage of the two.

findings.claim: MEADOWS LEVEL 6 (GAIN AROUND A REINFORCING LOOP) — the t1 judging loop has a measured gain of 1.00 then 1.14 and was stopped by a hand-issued owner ruling rather than by changing the gain, so the identical unguarded loop shape is still queued against a 7,381-frame corpus.

| wave | judged | new t1 | new t2 | tier ratio |
| A | 45 t2 | 0 | 6 | t2→t2 **0.13** |
| B | 21 t1 | 21 | 24 | t1→t1 **1.00** |
| C | 30 t2 | 0 | 11 | t2→t2 **0.37** |

t2 decays fast and emits **no overturn-claimers at all**. t1 is a **fixed point** at
~1.0–1.14: every overturn-claimer judged spawns roughly one more. It will never go dry, so
"loop until dry" is not available on this tier at any budget.

$ sed -n '193,196p' docs/GAUNTLET.md
5. **LOOP UNTIL DRY.** Keep spawning finders until **two consecutive rounds
   surface nothing new**. Dedup against everything *seen*, not everything
   *confirmed* — otherwise critic-rejected findings reappear each round and the
   loop never converges.

The engine's only stated stopping rule is 'until dry'. On a loop with gain >= 1 that instruction is unsatisfiable, so the loop ran four waves and then required a HUMAN RULING to terminate. RESUME_HERE flags the same shape as still live: 'l0-finish-wf4 ... Caps at 4 rounds ... one hunt target is the 7,381-frame corpus, which may never go dry' — 13-25 agents already queued against it.

WHY LEVEL 6 AND NOT LEVEL 1: the fix that first suggests itself is a round cap or an agent budget — a NUMBER, Meadows level 1, the weakest lever there is, and WF-4 already has one (4 rounds) which is precisely why it will report a false 'capped' rather than a true 'fixed point'. The gain itself is the lever: t2 emits ZERO overturn-claimers and decays at 0.13-0.37, t1 emits ~1.0-1.14 of its own kind. The loop's gain is a property of what the tier is ALLOWED to emit, and that is changeable.
findings.rule_targeted: docs/GAUNTLET.md §3 item 5 'LOOP UNTIL DRY' (:193-196, 33 words measured)
findings.proposed_change:
REPLACE §3 item 5 with: '5. **LOOP UNTIL DRY — OR PROVE THE GAIN.** Spawn finders until two consecutive rounds surface nothing new, deduping against everything *seen*, not everything *confirmed*. Report emission÷judged each round: >= 1 for two rounds means a fixed point — bank and stop.' (38 words; +5 net.)
This converts a decision the owner had to make by hand on 2026-08-23 into a number the loop computes about itself — the level-6 move, not the level-1 one. The dedup-on-SEEN clause is §1-proven and is preserved verbatim.
INCIDENT IT WOULD HAVE PREVENTED: waves B and D (commit ab93692) ran to completion before anyone split emissions by tier and discovered the fixed point; the stop then cost an owner ruling (71b612d) instead of firing automatically after wave D's 1.14.
SECOND-ORDER CONSEQUENCE, HONESTLY STATED: a loop that can stop itself will sometimes stop on a transient spike — wave B's 2.14 was a genuine one-off from adding the contradiction lens, and a naive gain rule would have banked there and lost wave C and D's 41 findings. The 'two consecutive rounds' clause is what absorbs that, and it is why the rule reads '>= 1 for TWO rounds' rather than '>= 1'.
ROLLBACK: `git checkout 2df2f87 -- docs/GAUNTLET.md` restores the original 33 words.
